body:

	With the end of preseason, the 2026-2027 NFL regular season officially kicks off with its first week of games starting on Wednesday, Sept. 9. The first game of the season is New England Patriots vs. Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field in Seattle, Washington, with a start time of 8:20 p.m. ET/5:20 p.m. PT on NBC.

	Throughout the season, games broadcast live across NBC, ABC, CBS, ESPN, FOX and NFL Network, as well as livestreams on ESPN Unlimited, Paramount+, FOX One, Peacock, Prime Video and NFL+.


	Even without cable, you don’t have to miss any of the action. You can access games on NBC, ABC, CBS and FOX with affordable cable antennas, while football games are also available to stream online on a variety of platforms, such as Sling TV and Hulu + Live TV. However, the best ways for cord-cutters to tune into the action is with DirecTV.

	With the start of a new season, it’s likely matches may features a few of celebrities in attendance to support their favorite teams, like Kansas City Chiefs-fan Taylor Swift, Seattle Seahawks-fan Chris Pratt, Philadelphia Eagles-fan Bradley Cooper, Los Angeles Rams-fan Kendrick Lamar and others.

	Meanwhile, with the popularity of the NFL, games throughout the season are going to be big ratings draws for networks. Programming like Super Bowl LX was a big ratings hit earlier in 2026 with more than 125 million viewers watching the big game.

		

						
			
	

					DirecTV
	
					
		

										unlimited cloud DVR Included						

					DirecTV 		

	
		DirecTV is one of the best ways for cable-cutters to access live sports and TV from home.	
		
	

	Save up to $30 on signature packages with DirecTV. Priced at $59.99/month for the first month of service ($89.99/month afterwards), you get access to the streaming service’s “Entertainment” package for football on NBC, ABC, CBS, ESPN, FOX and NFL Network, along with over 90 local, broadcast and cable channels. The streamer comes with unlimited cloud DVR for recording programming, as well as an additional 105 channels from DirecTV’s “MyFree” networks.


		

						
			
	

					Sling TV
	
					
		

										50+ Channels						

					Sling TV		

	
		Pricing and channel availability are subject to your local TV market.	
		
	

	Sling TV is one of the best options for affordable live streaming with the Sling Orange + Blue package starting at $69.99/month. The package includes NBC, ABC, ESPN, FOX and NFL Network, as well as more than 50 other channels. Plans include 50 hours of cloud DVR for recording programming and a library of free-to-watch on-demand movies and TV shows. Unfortunately, Sling TV doesn’t include CBS.

					Fubo

	Fubo is one of the best options for streaming football games live. The service features NBC, ABC, CBS, ESPN, FOX and NFL Network for football games. It even has more than 220 live TV channels for cable-free streaming and an unlimited cloud DVR. Watch the event with Fubo’s five-day free trial. You can even stream on up to two devices at the same time.

		

						
			
	

					Hulu
	
					
		

										Comes with Hulu, DIsney+ and ESPN Unlimited						

					Hulu + Live TV		

	
		Prices start at $89.99/month.	
		
	

	For great streaming option for to watch football, check out Hulu + Live TV for live channel streaming with access to NBC, ABC, CBS, ESPN, FOX and NFL Network. Starting at $89.99/month, the streaming service has more than 100 other channels, as well as access to hit originals on Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited.

		

						
			
	

					Amazon
	
					
		

										Home of ‘Thursday Night Football’						

					Prime Video		

		
	

	The NFL games throughout the season, namely “Thursday Night Football,” livestream on Prime Video.

	If you’re not a subscriber, you can sign up for a 30-day free trial to take advantage of all that Amazon Prime has to offer, including access to Prime Video and Prime Gaming; fast free shipping in less than two days with Prime Delivery; in-store discounts at Whole Foods Market, access to exclusive shopping events — like Prime Day and Black Friday — and more.

	You can purchase the livestream feed of the game starting at $8.99/month for the standalone Prime Video plan, or $139.99/year when you sign up for an annual Amazon Prime subscription here.

		

						
			
	

					ESPN
	
					
		

										Home of ‘Monday Night Football’						

					ESPN Unlimited		

	
		Get all ESPN networks with one streaming service	
		
	

	Get an ESPN Unlimited subscription here for $29.99/month, which will get you instant access to select NFL games, like “Monday Night Football,” livestream online. Unlike pay-per-view events, select NFL games are available to stream online free for ESPN Unlimited subscribers.

	For new subscribers, ESPN Unlimited bundle comes with Disney+ and Hulu for $35.99/month. The bundle comes with ESPN Unlimited, as well as Disney+ and Hulu for free when you purchase access to the livestream feed.

	However, the streaming service doesn’t come with a free trial, but there’s a clever workaround, if you want to watch ESPN Unlimited for free. Learn more about how to watch online for free here.


	ESPN Unlimited features everything that ESPN has to offer, including access to all of its networks and streaming service, like ESPN, ESPN2, ESPN3, ESPN on ABC, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network and ESPN+. It’s the ideal streamer for sports fans who want it all.

		

						
			
	

					Paramount+
	
					
		

										NFL on CBS						

					Paramount+		

	
		Prices start at $8.99/month	
		
	

	For new subscribers, Paramount+ starts at $8.99/month to access NFL on CBS.

	If you’re looking to livestream games, there is a clever workaround to get Paramount+ for cheap since the streamer doesn’t offer a free trial. Right now, you can sign up for a 30-day trial for Walmart+ for just $1. The retailer’s rewards program comes with Paramount+ as one of its perks.

	Aside from streaming access to select football games, you can take advantage of everything Walmart+ has to offer with perks such as free and fast delivery; fuel discounts at Walmart, Sam’s Club, Exxon, Mobil and Murphy stations; Burger King deals; additional savings with early access deals and many other perks. Learn more about what Walmart+ can offer you here.

		

						
			
	

					Fox Corp.
	
					
		

										NFL on FOX						

					FOX One		

		
	

	FOX has its own streaming service called FOX One, which features every network under the FOX umbrella, including FOX News, FOX Weather, FOX Nation, FOX Business, FOX Sports, FS2, Big Ten Network, FOX Deportes, FOX Network and your local FOX station. FOX One starts at $19.99/month ($199.99/year), or you can signup with the service as a channel add-on for Prime Video. In fact, go with Prime Video and get a three-day free trial just for signing up.

	Please note: You have to be a subscriber to Prime Video to get FOX One as an add-on channel.

		

						
			
	

					NBCUniversal
	
					
		

										Home of ‘Sunday Night Football’						

					Peacock		

		
	

	NFL games on NBC, like “Sunday Night Football,” livestream on Peacock, so the best way to watch is to purchase a subscription starting at $12.99/month here. Not a subscriber? You can get a Peacock monthly subscription to stream Premier League soccer matches online, and keep it to watch other hits, including “Obsession,” “The Wild Robot,” “How To Train Your Dragon,” “Reminders of Him,” “The Traitors,” “Vanderpump Rules” and others.

	In addition, the NFL+ streaming service is a must. It features all games across broadcast and cable networks during the regular season, postseason, preseason and even Super Bowl LXI. It broadcasts 24 hours of everything NFL starting at $6.99/month. Learn more about NFL+ here.


	The best way to livestream the 2026-27 NFL season is with a subscription to DirecTV, below. It’s the most comprehensive overall.

	Select games throughout the season livestreams on Netflix too. For a complete 2026-2027 NFL season schedule, click here.

title: ‘Entourage’ Creator Slams ‘God-Awful’ Ad Reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier: A ‘S—ty Imitation’ That ‘Makes Me Puke’
description: “Entourage” creator Doug Ellin has spoken out against an ad reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier, calling it a “cheap, shitty imitation” of his
body:
“Entourage” creator Doug Ellin has spoken out against an ad reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier, calling it a “cheap, shitty imitation” of his beloved HBO comedy.

	While Piven and Grenier are technically playing themselves in the ad — not super agent Ari Gold and movie star Vincent Chase — their performances, dialogue and dynamic are certainly reminiscent of “Entourage.” (Piven snakes his way through a mansion party to find Grenier on a yacht, where he pitches him a new movie role.)
	

	“Many people worked really hard to make our show as good as it was,” Ellin wrote on Instagram. “When I see cheap, shitty imitations that try to pass for what we did it makes me puke.”


	On Wednesday, Variety broke the news of Piven and Grenier’s on-screen reunion, which took place in a three-minute spot for Jake Paul’s gambling app Betr. Ellin said in a video message that he received “400 messages” about the “god-awful commercial,” clarifying that he was not involved in its creation.

	Ellin said he’s not bitter over not being paid for the ad. He simply wishes the writers of “Entourage” would get more credit for the hard work they put into the scripts and character development, only for their work to be distilled into an “embarrassing” emulation of the HBO hit.

	“I watch it and I want to throw up, because I would suffer, along with many other people, over every syllable, every fucking word,” Ellin said. “So I watch this trash, this shit, and go, ‘Ugh, ugh.’ There’s no bitterness. I want everyone to get paid, get rich. Just fucking do your own shit. That’s all.”
	

	Ellin then seemed to take a shot at Piven — who won three Emmys for playing Ari on the series — claiming that the actor distanced himself from “Entourage” in the years following the 2011 series finale and 2015 movie.

	“I not only wrote, we found these people. We cast these people,” Ellin said of forming the “Entourage” ensemble. “I actually had to beg Piven to do the show because he didn’t wanna do it. And he didn’t wanna talk about it afterwards. Like, he wanted to get away from it, because he had so much better shit going on. But now he’s back on it, because he’s getting paid.”

	A representative for Piven did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment.

	Responding to Ellin’s comments, a spokesperson for Betr said in a statement, “We were excited to bring Jeremy and Adrian back together, appearing as themselves. Creating that kind of unexpected cultural moment with two amazing actors was exactly what we wanted for Betr 2.0.”

	The statement continues, “We’re really proud of how the spot came together, and the response has been overwhelmingly positive, generating nearly 10 million organic social views in less than 24 hours. We had a lot of fun making it, they had a lot of fun making it, and people seem to be having a lot of fun watching it. We appreciate Doug watching the ad and helping promote it. Betr 2.0 is available now.”

	On another social media app, X, Ellin continued to lash out against the ad. “I have zero positivity in watching things I busted my ass [off] on for years [be] turned into garbage,” he wrote. “Go create your own shit. And if you need money … Flip burgers. This is trash and theft. Period.”

	Responding to a fan who said he hoped Ellin was behind the ad, the “Entourage” creator fired back: “I think it’s pretty damn obvious I didn’t write it. My god.” And, with apparent sarcasm, Ellin replied to a fan asking for an “Entourage” reboot: “Piven should write and direct. I can’t wait [to] watch.”

	Ellin has often been asked about doing an “Entourage” reboot since the series ended 15 years ago. A proper revival has never been in development, but the cast and (for a while) Ellin have expressed an interest in returning to the world of Vinny Chase. Earlier this month, however, Ellin threw cold water on the possibility, saying on the “Joe Vulpis Podcast” that a reboot or spinoff is unlikely, and “I don’t spend one second thinking about ideas unless somebody’s paying me.”
	

	The closest he got to a revival was a 2022 pilot titled “Ramble On,” a dramedy about established stars looking to reinvent their careers that starred “Entourage” favorites including Kevin Connolly and Kevin Dillon alongside Charlie Sheen. Ellin released the trailer for the project, but it ultimately failed to sell to a distributor.

	Ellin currently hosts the “Victory” podcast with “Entourage” star Kevin Dillon.

title: Chernin Entertainment Expands Film Team With Key Hire, Promotions (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Chernin Entertainment, the prolific independent film and TV producer founded by former News Corp. chairman Peter Chernin, has expanded its in-house
body:
Chernin Entertainment, the prolific independent film and TV producer founded by former News Corp. chairman Peter Chernin, has expanded its in-house film team.

	Under movies chief David Ready, the film unit has had big wins this year in theaters (“Backrooms”) and on streaming (Netflix’s “The Last House”), and will continue to scale its slate.

	To fulfill that effort is new hire Marisa Paiva, who joins as an executive vice president of film. Paiva got her start Fox 2000 and spent over 13 years at the studio, working on literary adaptations like “Water for Elephants” and “Life of Pi.” She later oversaw the award-winning “Hidden Figures” and “The Woman in the Window.” She joined 3000 Pictures in 2019, developing “Lady Chatterley’s Lover” for Netflix and spearheading high-profile acquisitions like “Broken Country,” which Paiva will executive produce with Hello Sunshine.
	

	Paiva will join fellow EVP Brady Fujikawa, who joined the studio last year from Lionsgate. Fujikawa rises from his previous title of development and production lead. He oversaw the hot package “High Side,” which will put Timothée Chalamet in a motocross seat for director James Mangold. Fujikawa is also shepherding “Palm Grove,” starring Kate Hudson and Ana de Armas and directed by Kornél Mundruczó; and “One Month Mark,” a Jennifer Lawrence rom-com set up at Apple. He was previously at Good Universe (“Blockers,” “Good Boys”), and helped expand the John Wick universe at Lionsgate.


	Meanwhile, Samantha Nisenboim has been named senior vice president of film. Her producer credits include “The Lego Batman Movie,” The Tomorrow War” and “Renfield.” She is currently producing two feature films at Chernin, including the Netflix thriller “The Big Fix” starring Mark Wahlberg and Riz Ahmed. 
	

	Finally, Max Gains has been named creative executive. He began his career at Paramount before joining 21 Laps, where he spent six years working his way up from Shawn Levy’s assistant. His projects included “Deadpool & Wolverine,” “The Adam Project” and “Free Guy.”

	Ready told Variety that the company has “built a strong foundation and a slate we really believe in, and now we have the team to build out our next chapter. Marisa, Brady, Samantha, and Max are the kind of executives you want on your team – smart, relentless, deeply connected and driven by great material.”

	Chernin recently inked a new multi-year, first-look feature film deal with Apple Studios. In January, Mediawan announced an agreement to acquire Chernin parent The North Road Company. The combined entity will have major creative hubs across five continents and capabilities spanning all genres and formats.

schema.headline: Chernin Entertainment Expands Film Team With Key Hire, Promotions (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Company’ Review: Casey Affleck’s Latest Directorial Effort Isn’t What It Initially Appears to Be, but Isn’t Very Interesting Either Way
description: Stories are nested within stories to steadily diminishing returns in “Company,” a perversely ponderous exercise in hide-the-genre that takes more th
body:
Stories are nested within stories to steadily diminishing returns in “Company,” a perversely ponderous exercise in hide-the-genre that takes more than an hour to reveal what its game really is. Gathering little tension ahead of a ludicrous twist — one that puts proceedings in a new light while adding no great urgency to them — Casey Affleck’s second feature as writer-director feels altogether less assured than his 2019 debut, the somberly effective post-apocalyptic drama “Light of My Life.” This time staying behind the camera entirely, and handing a demanding lead role to his teenage son Atticus, Affleck again brings an earnest seriousness of purpose to this staggered tale of a mysterious stranger drifting into a household and holding it eerily rapt, repeated across three different eras. But for all the echoey narrative tripling here, the payoff is distinctly muted.
	

	“Company” presents a significant challenge to the marketing teams of any distributors taking it on after its Venice competition premiere — though given the dull peculiarity of the film, coupled with a muted festival reception, said distributors are by no means a given. How does one pitch to audiences a film where its grabbiest story hook is also its most carefully guarded secret? Minus the surprise factor that certainly caught Venice journalists off guard, viewers going in with some idea of what’s coming will be even more perplexed by the coy obfuscation and molasses pacing of the film’s first two-thirds, which mostly present as the kind of melancholically revisionist period Western one might expect from the star of “The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford” and “The World to Come.” (And indeed his co-scripter Ron Hansen, writer of the former film’s source novel and the latter film’s screenplay.)
	

	It begins in the year 1975, as Evelyn (Emily Alyn Lind), a quietly self-possessed, soberly dressed young woman, arrives on the doorstep of a well-to-do suburban home, in the midst of an almighty downpour. (Bob Dylan’s “Shelter From the Storm” is the opening soundtrack cue; it turns out to be lyrically on the nose in multiple ways.) Not recognizing the name Evelyn asks for, the man who answers the door says she has the wrong address, but invites her in to dry off; they’re having a Christmas party, and several of the guests are intrigued by the reserved, well-spoken stranger, who offers to regale them with a story.

	In the recursive manner of the old “it was a dark and stormy night” chestnut, Evelyn’s story soon teases viewers (and listeners) with some déjà vu: Set in 1953, it tells of elderly rural widower Tom (a maximally grizzled Nick Nolte), who finds an enigmatic young woman, Alice (Caylee Cowan) collapsed in the snow near his cabin in the Colorado mountains, and brings her inside to warm up. In return for his hospitality, she offers to tell him a story — about Rebecca (Adelaide Clemens) and Emmett (Scoot McNairy), a hardscrabble Colorado farming couple in 1903, who find young drifter Caleb (Atticus Affleck) unconscious in the snow, and carry him home to recover.

	This tedious roundelay of story introductions mercifully ends here, as the turn-of-the-century tale becomes the film’s primary focus, though fear not: Its principals still have plenty of stories to tell. Rebecca, a patient salt-of-the-earth type, is compelled by the surly, coldly withholding Caleb, and invites him to stay on as a hired hand. Emmett, wary from the start, would rather see the back of him, and his suspicions grow when word spreads of a series of brutal murders in the area. At this point, it’s impossible to discuss the film without any mention of its true identity, so potential viewers wishing to preserve the unspoiled viewing experience would be advised to stop reading here.

	In all three timelines, a slightly unsettling stranger — clad in severe monochrome tailoring — is let into an unsuspecting home, and by the time bloody violence enters the equation, the clues check out: This is, like “Sinners,” a period heartland vampire movie that uses the mythic conventions of that genre to say something or other about the American spirit of community, or lack thereof. “Company,” however, peddles some wildly divergent vampire lore to ultimately announce itself as a fable on the nature of human, or inhuman, kindness: Its bloodthirsty raconteurs are capable of grace and mercy when treated with same, which is certainly a novel mythos within this rich and varied storytelling tradition, if not a terribly exciting one.
	

	Caleb, at least, has a bit of attitude, and what tension “Company” generates largely rests on his still, pale-eyed, tacitly judgmental presence. In an extended verbal confrontation between him and neighboring farmer Kleinschmidt (a caustic, quick-on-the-draw Ben Mendelsohn, by several notches the ensemble’s MVP), Affleck and Hansen’s dourly lyrical dialogue finally crackles with something like foreboding. As Caleb, the younger Affleck — who resembles, in features and affect, the love child of Timothée Chalamet and Troye Sivan — occasionally lets his inexperience show, though there’s genuine mystery in his willowy insolence; only when he’s on screen does “Company” have a welcome whisper of danger to it.

	Elsewhere, it simply plays as a protracted shaggy-dog tease with no sense of humor, and an inflated sense of its own poetry. Affleck continues to demonstrate promising filmmaking chops: He can conjure starkly mournful atmosphere aplenty, and the film is handsome in an appropriately ascetic, chambray-textured way. Yet perhaps the most puzzling thing about “Company” — more so, even, than its surprise vampires — is why it boasts a whopping eight DPs, including such accomplished, distinctive stylists as Masanobu Takayanagi (“Springsteen: Deliver Me From Nowhere”), Adam Arkapaw (“Macbeth”) and Marcell Rév (“White God”), as well as Affleck himself. If the plan was to give each of the film’s enfolded narratives its own characterizing aesthetic, that isn’t clear in the film’s earthy visual consistency. If it’s a tell of an addled or waylaid production, the final film doesn’t seem entirely worth the trouble. Many hands don’t make light work of “Company”; many tellers don’t make one good story.

schema.headline: ‘Company’ Review: Casey Affleck’s Latest Directorial Effort Isn’t What It Initially Appears to Be, but Isn’t Very Interesting Either Way

title: How Netflix Will Use Apple’s iPhone Duo to Deliver a ‘Big-Screen Feeling’
description:
Sep 9, 2026 1:31pm PT	
	

	
		How Netflix Will Use Apple’s iPhone Duo to Deliver a ‘Big-Screen Feeling’
body:
Sep 9, 2026 1:31pm PT	
	

	
		How Netflix Will Use Apple’s iPhone Duo to Deliver a ‘Big-Screen Feeling’
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Courtesy of Apple
	

		
	
				
	Apple has unveiled its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, which has a 7.6-inch diagonal screen when opened up. And Netflix is here for it.

	Netflix is among the handful of pre-release partners who have been working with Apple to redesign their iOS apps for the larger screen real estate of the iPhone Duo and to take advantage of its new interface features.

	“When members use Netflix on iOS, they want that same immersive, big-screen feeling to travel with them,” a company spokesperson told Variety. The streamer’s upcoming iOS 27 version of the app designed for the iPhone Duo “reimagines Billboard, our new playback controls and Clips for the new device.”
	

	Here are details on what to expect from Netflix’s Duo-optimized app:


Billboard: For the new iOS experience on iPhone Duo, Netflix is implementing a version of Billboard — the interactive promotional card feature at the top of the mobile interface — that “brings entertainment to life in your hands.” The new iteration of Billboard features “dynamic visual effects enhanced by the display,” Netflix says.
Clips: The Netflix app’s Clips, a TikTok-style vertical video feed with snippets from shows and movies, can use the device’s wide screen, “switching seamlessly and frame-accurately between vertical and horizontal so your phone adapts to what you’re watching and how you want to enjoy it.”
Playback: Netflix has redesigned the player for iPhone Duo so its controls “move with you, adapting seamlessly no matter how you’re watching – full screen, folded or propped up,” the company says. When propped up especially, Netflix “rethought how controls should behave alongside our members, so they stay intuitive and within reach no matter how you’re interacting with the device,” the company says. In addition, Netflix added a “subtle, reflective glow” to the controls that responds to ambient light and the angle of the device; that’s a “small touch that pulls you just a little deeper into whatever you’re watching,” per the streamer.



	The iPhone Duo is priced starting at $1,999 with 256 gigabytes of storage, and costs up to $3,199 for a model with 2 terabytes. Preorders start Oct. 16 and the device will begin shipping Oct. 23.

	SEE ALSO: Apple Introduces iPhone Duo, Its First Foldable Smartphone
	


	
		More from Variety

schema.headline: How Netflix Will Use Apple’s iPhone Duo to Deliver a ‘Big-Screen Feeling’

title: ‘The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’ 40th Anniversary Remake Sets Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date (Gaming News Roundup)
description: Celebrating 40 years of gameplay, an updated version of “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” will be available for Nintendo Switch 2 on Nov. 5.
body:
Celebrating 40 years of gameplay, an updated version of “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” will be available for Nintendo Switch 2 on Nov. 5.

	The remake will have overhauled visuals, fully voiced cutscenes, expanded character dialogue, symphonic orchestral music, reworked camera and movement controls and more. In this game, the main playable protagonist, Link’s, milestone adventure has been reborn for a whole new era. 


	This version of “Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” will have improved performance and presentation, greater movement and control and a more immersive Hyrule. Players can now sing or hum one of Link’s learned ocarina melodies within range of the Nintendo Switch 2 system’s built-in microphone, and he’ll perform the song in the game. 
	

	For additional information about new features and enhancements coming to “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time” or to preorder, please visit Nintendo Store or Nintendo eShop.

	See more gaming news from the week below.
	
		TRAILERS 	

	“Spyro: A Realm Beyond” has released its first look at Arcadian Vale in honor of Spyro Community Day. 

	The game’s region is a calm, vibrant location consisting of natural beauty. Per the game’s description, “Across the scene are cascading waterfalls tumbling down from towering cliffs. Ancient stone structures and weathered monuments rise from the terrain while lush greenery blankets the valley floor, creating a destination that feels magical and alive.”

	Also featuring friendly creatures, Arcadian Vale is designed to capture the whimsy of the “Spyro” universe. 
	

	See the first look below.


	
		NEWLY ANNOUNCED GAMES 	

	Nintendo unveiled “Metroid Ravenous” and “Kirby and the World Beyond” during a Nintendo Direct presentation Wednesday, noting both newly announced games will be available on the Nintendo Switch 2 next year.

	Samus Aran is back with even more of a fight for survival in “Metroid Ravenous.” The game’s amiibo collection will feature Samus and Chozo Statue figures at its launch, while a third amiibo of Samus in her Metroid Suit will be bundled in a special edition that also includes a steel case for the game. Both releases will launch Jan. 28, and pre-orders are available now. 

	“Kirby and the World Beyond” is a 3D adventure for Kirby, where the character’s Copy Abilities allow players to freely explore Kirby’s universe. The game will debut in spring 2027, timed with the 35th anniversary for the Kirby series.

	See first look photos below. 



	

	





	

	


	
		EVENTS	

	PAX West is returning to the Seattle Convention Center next Labor Day weekend from Sept. 3 to Sept. 6, following this year’s event. 

	The gaming event will also debut PAX Unplugged Houston, the new iteration of PAX expos that will take place June 25 to June 27 at the George R. Brown Convention Center in Houston, Texas. Badges will be available to purchase later this year. 

	On the East Coast, PAX Unplugged 2026 returns to the Pennsylvania Convention Center Dec. 6 to Dec. 8, while PAX East 2027 will be held in Boston at the Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center April 22 to April 25.
	
		LIVE EVENTS	

	Select AMC theaters will screen the live broadcast of Epic Games’ 2026 Rocket League World Championship Finals. 

	For the first time, fans will be able to watch Rocket League teams compete for the $1.2 million prize pool on Sept. 20 at 50 AMC locations nationwide, including Chicago, Boston, New York and Los Angeles. The event is estimated to run for approximately eight hours, and tickets are on sale now. Attendees will also receive a commemorative Rocket League ticket that allows players to redeem in-game cosmetics. 

	“Such a big part of the magic of movie theaters is their ability to bring people together for unforgettable shared experiences, and a live event like the Rocket League World Championship is a great example of that,” said Ellen Copaken, the senior vice president of business development at AMC Theatres. “We’re excited to give fans the opportunity to watch esports’ biggest stage unfold live on massive screens, surrounded by fellow Rocket League fans.”

schema.headline: ‘The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’ 40th Anniversary Remake Sets Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date (Gaming News Roundup)

title: Channing Dungey on Warner Bros. TV Group’s Big Year of Pickups, Renewals and New Deals — Despite Industry Distractions and Ownership Uncertainty
description: Warner Bros. TV Group isn’t acting like a studio with an uncertain future. Even as the fate of Warner Bros. Discovery remains up in the air — given
body:
Warner Bros. TV Group isn’t acting like a studio with an uncertain future. Even as the fate of Warner Bros. Discovery remains up in the air — given the uncertain timeline of a Paramount Skydance acquisition — the studio has been on a development and production spree in recent months.

	This summer the division, under chairman Channing Dungey, reupped its megadeal with John Wells — whose hit juggernaut for HBO Max, “The Pitt,” already won four Emmys last weekend and is expected to dominate the drama category at Monday night’s main ceremony.
	

	Also, Variety can exclusively reveal that Matt Reeves and his 6th & Idaho production shingle (“The Penguin”) have reupped their overall deal with Warner Bros. TV. Reeves and company first signed on in 2020 to produce all TV projects with the studio. (“Matt has a true knack for getting into the psyche of his characters and he and his team have delivered some of the most compelling, thought-provoking stories over the years,” Dungey says.)


	Other overall deals housed at the company include prolific creators like Greg Berlanti, Bill Lawrence, Chuck Lorre, Mindy Kaling, Lucia Aniello/Paul W. Downs and Jen Statsky.

	Meanwhile, since January, the studio has landed 12 new series orders — most recently, the long-awaited revival of the “Manifest” franchise at Netflix, “Arrivals: A New Manifest Mystery.” Warner Bros. also lined up pickups for scripted series such as the DC-themed true-crime mockumentary “The People v. Gorilla Grodd” at HBO Max; the Brett Goldstein romantic comedy “Escorted” and horror drama “Stillwater” at Prime Video; the reimagined comic “Afterlife With Archie” at Disney+; and sitcom “I Suck at Girls” at Netflix.
	

	Then there are the dozen series that have been renewed in recent months: “The Pitt,” “It: Welcome to Derry,” “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” and “Rooster” at HBO Max, “Leanne,” “Untamed” and “Running Point” at Netflix, “Shrinking” and “Bad Monkey” at Apple TV, and broadcast hits “Memory of a Killer” (Fox) and “Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage” (CBS). At ABC, “Abbott Elementary,” the No. 1 broadcast comedy in multiplatform among adults 18-49, returns for Season 6 next month.

	And if that’s not enough, the studio is also spending big on the upcoming “Harry Potter” series it’s producing for sibling HBO Max; and it’s behind one of the most anticipated new series on Netflix in the coming year, “Scooby-Doo: Origins.”

	Dungey’s studio domain also includes unscripted fare (including new seasons of “The Real Housewives: New York City,” “The Real Housewives: Salt Lake City” and Season 30 of “The Voice”), syndication (“Extra” and “The Jennifer Hudson Show”) and animation (including recent orders for Genndy Tartakovsky’s “Heist Brothers” and Tubi’s “Yokoso Scooby-Doo”).

	As head of WBD U.S. networks, her oversight includes top 10 networks TBS, TNT, TLC and Food Network, and launched the No. 1 new unscripted series with TLC’s “Suddenly Amish.” Also this year, Discovery’s “Shark Week” had its best ratings since 2019, while “Puppy Bowl” scored its best audience in eight years across multiple platforms.

	“Certainly when I when I look up toward my boss and everything that’s happening on the corporate level, it’s a complicated time,” says Dungey. “But it is not impacting our day-to-day business in any real way… My focus is continuing to work with the best creatives, develop the best shows, find the best homes for them, and that’s all been happening.”

	Variety spoke with Dungey about the state of the studio and cable portfolio, and what’s next.
	
		Two seasons in, what have you learned from the success of “The Pitt?”	

	What we’ve discovered with “The Pitt” is two things: audiences really love the weekly drop. “The Pitt” isn’t alone in this. We drop “Ted Lasso” weekly, for example. I think that there is something about the event. I think you appreciate them more when you watch them one at a time as opposed to binge. But the other really significant thing is the idea that you have it on an annual cadence. People right now are losing their mind that we’re already putting out teaser trailers for “The Pitt” Season 3 when it feels like “The Pitt” Season 2 just ended. And that feels good to the audience. It keeps them engaged and it keeps them connected to these characters. When you’ve got 18, 20, 22 months between seasons, sometimes even longer, life goes on and you kind of forget. Like, “why did I like that show so much?” I am hopeful that more streamers will put effort into trying to bring shows back on an annual cadence.
	
	
		How did the “Manifest” spinoff finally happen?	

	“Manifest” original recipe did very well on Netflix, and there was a desire to continue to explore stories and ideas within that universe. It took a little bit for [creator] Jeff [Rake] and team to nail the right way to approach the concept. Even though it’s taken a little bit of time, I think we’ve now built something else that has a really great long-running engine at its core.
	
		How much does the new show play off the old one? Is it a continuation of the story?	

	It was very important to Netflix that people who never watched the original could dive in and appreciate it on its own. But if you were a hardcore fan of the original, there’s enough connective tissue and mythology and Easter eggs that reward you for having been a part of this universe for such a long time. That’s part of why it was a little tricky to figure out exactly how we wanted to build it.
	
		Will there be any cameos from the original cast?	

	Possibly. There’s definitely room for some of that if we choose to. But at this point there aren’t any big plans to do that.
	
		There’s been a lot of conversation lately about the difficulty with Season 2 drop-offs on some of the streamers.	

	It’s always been hard. Back in the day, I always would say, getting through Season 2 is always the toughest. Because things launch, they’re new, they’re exciting, you’ve got a plethora of stories to tell. Then you have to do that all over again in Season 2 … And then it’s a one-two punch if you take forever to bring it back and then you drop all the episodes and you watch it all in a matter of days. It’s hard to remain part of the conversation.
	
		You were looking to replicate that regular “Pitt”-like cadence with the police drama “American Blue,” which was passed on by HBO Max. How’s the search going to find it a new home?	

	We still have a couple of bites. We have the finished pilot, and we have another five scripts done to follow it. So if one of these places picks it up, we’ll be ready to rock ‘n’ roll. And we also still have “How to Survive Without Me,” which is the other pilot that we did in contention at Max. That is also the “Pitt” model, but the relationship drama version. It’s Greg Berlanti doing what he did so well with shows like “Brothers and Sisters,” with Ray Romano and Josh Jackson and Kaley Cuoco.
	
	
		What’s the word on that one?	

	We should be getting some word imminently. We’re waiting on another script to go into Max, and hopefully that’s the thing that says “greenlight, go.”
	
		Most recently, Hulu canceled Mindy Kaling’s “Not Suitable for Work” after just a season. I know you’re looking to shop it around. How difficult is that? A few years ago a show like that would have been given a second season or would have quickly found a second home on another streamer.	

	Every platform has their needs and they know what’s going on internally. “Not Suitable for Work” is a tremendous show. I love that cast so much. I’m very hopeful that we land a second season somewhere else. But it’s tough, especially with comedy, you really have to develop that relationship with the characters, and it takes time.
	
		As for “Ted Lasso,” does Jason Sudeikis have another three-season arc? How much of it is mapped out?	

	We haven’t heard any creative beyond the season that we are finishing editorial on right now. When you get to the end of this season, I think you can see that it could go either way. There’s definitely branching narrative that could continue forward, and if Season 4 becomes the end, then I think it’s satisfying in its own way too.
	
		Is that a Jason call? An Apple call? Who are we waiting on to see if there will be a Season 5?	

	With this, it’s always a complicated conversation. I think you can say it’s a little bit of everybody.
	
		With the success of “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe,” how far can you take “The Big Bang Theory” franchise? More series?	

	This is such a rare gift, right? To have a multi-camera comedy give birth to a single-camera comedy, then to a multi-camera comedy, and back to a single. I don’t think it’s ever been done before that hat trick in exactly that way, I’m really excited that we’re going to be doing a second season. I don’t know if Chuck has another idea in his back pocket for how to extend this universe further, but I’ll certainly be the first in line to hear it if he does.
	
		Let’s talk about your expectations for “Harry Potter” as we get closer to Christmas. This is going to be unlike most launches that you’ve experienced.	

	Oh, 100%. I’ve never been a part of a of a show this big, in terms of the way this world has been realized. The opportunity that we’ve had to really bring the books to life in the fullest of ways because we’re not limited by a running time in that way has been really exciting and I think will be really rewarding for audiences.
	
	
		What’s it like to be working on a project where you know it’s going to be going on for years? You can spread out costs and plot things out.	

	Casey and I joke about this. You feel sort of like you’re the people at the beginning of the marathon carrying the baton, and you’re going to run as far as you go, and then you’re going to hand it to somebody else. Because I mean, this is probably another decade from here. But it’s really been fun to be here at the beginning and to help bring this all to life. 
	
		Has any of the corporate uncertainty changed the way you can greenlight a show?	

	We have not run up against any of those problems or challenges in terms of programming. Certainly as a largely independent studio, we are still buying projects and selling them to all different platforms at all different times. I have not seen any impact in terms of the decisions that Casey [Bloys] and the team are making on the HBO Max side either. And in terms of what we’re doing with the U.S. Nets, most of that programming is done on an annual cadence. We’re well into our buying for ‘27 and ‘28 and all of that is moving forward.
	
		What’s the biggest thing you’ve had to actually put on hold or adjust?	

	We haven’t really put anything on hold. I think that if this deal continues to go on, we may soon. With some of these longer-term overall deals, it’s not that you’re putting anything on pause, but if you’re going to be making a big long-term commitment, certainly we’re going to want to discuss that with our partners across the aisle.
	
		Have you found that the threshold for green lights has changed at all in the business?	

	In terms of green lights and acquisitions around town, I think that most of the platforms that we work with, everyone is being a little bit more scrutinous about what they want to buy, what they want to invest in. There was a period a few years ago where it felt like people were ordering everything straight to series off a pitch. And now it’s a little bit more like, “We’d like to see a couple of scripts, maybe three scripts. We want to hear the series pitch for the season before we commit.” And I think it just reflects the fact that everyone’s slates are a little more compressed than they were. People are being much more deliberate about the decisions that they make,
	
	
		How would you describe the state of development in the industry right now?	

	It’s been pretty consistent. 2022, 2023 was the beginning of a little bit of a contraction in the business as a whole. And certainly around that time, broadcast got extra skinny. That impacts the number of projects that you’re developing. But I feel like since that time we’ve remained pretty level year over year.
	
		How are budgets looking now? You’re producing what I imagine is one of the most expensive shows on television with ‘Harry Potter.’	

	I think everybody is being a bit more fiscally responsible than they were in that really boom, bonanza time. In the pre-COVID time it did feel like there was almost a freewheeling attitude toward it, especially from some of the streamers. I don’t think you feel that anymore. We’re spending what we need to spend to make the best possible shows at all different price points.
	
		Sam Register is leaving as head of Warner Bros. Animation, Cartoon Network Studios and Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe. Are you able to fill that position, or do you have to wait for the ownership issue to be resolved?	

	That’s absolutely a role that we’ll be looking to fill. Sam built such an incredible team, and the creatives who have been working with Sam for so many years are all still in place. I do want to tap a new leader of the division. We shared the news with Paramount that Sam was going to be departing, but there is no impediment to filling that role.
	
		Now that you’ve been in charge of the U.S. network for a while, how have your thoughts about the future of linear evolved? Can they continue to be programmed as cable networks or at some point do they become more seen as content engines for HBO Max and streaming platforms?	

	It’s an interesting question and I think it’s both — meaning, there is still a very loyal dedicated audience watching these cable networks on linear. We’re having ratings growth on Food. We launched two new shows, “24 in 24” and “100 Cooks,” that both broke through without having some of our big-name talent attached to them. So there is still a lot of real meaningful growth in linear. But we’ve spent a lot of time talking internally about the fact that in this current day and age, we can’t just think about these networks as linear networks. We do have to think about them as brands, and how can we extend and enhance these brands. So many of them have great consumer connection. Especially when you think about HGTV and Food. People are more likely to buy a can of paint if it has the HGTV logo on it. They’re more likely to download a recipe if it has the Food Network logo on it.
	
	
		Do you ever think about where they might fit in and be integrated with the Paramount cable networks?	

	There are definitely some networks that they have that I think could work very nicely with some of ours. The opportunity for growth as you pull things together is potentially very exciting. I am hopeful that there will be a point where we can actually engage in some of these conversations. But for now, it’s all theoretical.
	
		Have you had any conversations with David Ellison about the company, Warner Bros. TV and the cable networks?	

	I’ve had a couple of meetings with David, but more of a “getting to know you” on both sides and less of “Here’s the vision for the structure in the future.” It’s too early in the process for those conversations.
	
		Would you like to remain a part of this company post-merger?	

	I love my team at Warner Bros. Television Group. I love our shows, our talent. And I’ve become very happy in my U.S. networks role, which was something that I didn’t see coming almost two years ago. The best-case scenario for me is something that allows me to continue to play around in both of these spaces.

schema.headline: Channing Dungey on Warner Bros. TV Group’s Big Year of Pickups, Renewals and New Deals — Despite Industry Distractions and Ownership Uncertainty

title: ‘Charlie’s Angels’ Reunion, Zendaya and ‘Buffy’ Alums Sarah Michelle Gellar, David Boreanaz Among Confirmed Emmys Presenters
description: “Charlie’s Angels” and “Angel” are among the first round of names announced Wednesday to serve as presenters at Monday night’s 78th Emmys on NBC and
body:
“Charlie’s Angels” and “Angel” are among the first round of names announced Wednesday to serve as presenters at Monday night’s 78th Emmys on NBC and Peacock.

	“Charlie’s Angels” stars Kate Jackson, Cheryl Ladd and Jaclyn Smith — who are celebrating the 50th anniversary this year of the iconic ABC series — were included in the list of presenters, so an on-stage reunion of the three is a given. The trio earlier this year also got together to mark the show’s 50th at a PaleyFest panel in Hollywood.
	

	Another “Angel” — this time, David Boreanaz, the star of the “Buffy the Vampire Slayer” spinoff “Angel,” was also announced — along with “Buffy” star Sarah Michelle Gellar, so perhaps they, too, will be paired on stage. (Boreanaz is also there to promote his new NBC drama remake of “The Rockford Files.”)


	Other presenters set to join in are “DTF St. Louis” stars Linda Cardellini and David Harbour, who won Emmys last weekend for outstanding limited/anthology actress and actor, respectively. Their categories were originally slated to air during the NBC telecast, but were later moved to Night 2 of the show — causing some backlash. But now, their wins will be properly recognized at the ceremony.

	Additional names set to hit the stage on Monday: Odessa A’zion, Macaulay Culkin, Alan Cumming, Sally Field, Jon Hamm, Marcello Hernández, Peter Krause, Dan Levy, Julianna Margulies, Annie Murphy, Niecy Nash-Betts, Keke Palmer, Amanda Peet, Amy Poehler, Florence Pugh, Rachel Sennott and Zendaya.

	Cumming won an Emmy over the weekend for outstanding host for a reality or reality competition program; he’s also up for the reality competition Emmy on Monday. (He’s so far won five Emmys overall.) 
	

	Field is nominated for lead actres in a limited/anthology series or movie; her Netflix film “Remarkably Bright Creatures” won for outstanding movie over the weekend. If she wins, at age 79 she will become the oldest winner ever in the category.

	Zendaya, meanwhile, is up for drama lead actress for “Euphoria.” If she wins, she’ll become the youngest performer ever to win three lead drama Emmys.

	More presenters will be announced at a later date, NBC and the TV Academy said.

	The 78th Emmys broadcast live from the Peacock Theater at LA Live on Monday, Sept. 14, at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on NBC and Peacock.

	“Law & Order SVU” star/exec producer Mariska Hargitay, who won two Emmys over the weekend for her doc “My Mom Jayne,” is host. Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay of Jesse Collins Entertainment and Mariska Hargitay will serve as executive producers of the telecast.

title: Taylor Swift Has Never Won a Grammy for Record or Song of the Year. With Three No. 1 Hits Eligible for 2027, Which Will She Choose for Victory?
description: There are two points of view you could take on Taylor Swift and her Grammys history: (a) Swift has been a Grammys hoarder. (b) Swift has gotten robb
body:
There are two points of view you could take on Taylor Swift and her Grammys history: (a) Swift has been a Grammys hoarder. (b) Swift has gotten robbed by the Recording Academy… regularly. Which of these contradictory statements is true?

	How about both of them? They’re not actually as oxymoronic as they appear; it just depends which categories you’re considering. On the one hand, Swift is the all-time top honoree when it comes to Album of the Year, having picked it up four times (for “Fearless,” “1989,” “Folklore” and “Midnights,” spread out over a period of 14 years). She got so much attention for that record-shattering four-peat that there may be a popular perception that she’s already won enough Grammys for one person’s lifetime. In all, she’s picked up 14.
	

	But here’s what very few people realize, or remember: She has never won Record of the Year or Song of the Year. That’s not a misprint. The biggest pop music star of the 21st century, and the one with the most No. 1 Hot 100 hits this century — 15 — has never been rewarded in either of the two all-genre Grammy categories that honor singles. Whether you love her, can’t stand her or fall somewhere in-between, that oversight for someone who is quantifiably the modern era’s most reliable crafter of indelible songs is kind of flabbergasting to consider.


	Now, if things had to be that lopsided, and Swift had to pick just one of the Grammys’ top three categories in which to be such a dominative force, she’d probably say she was happy where she landed. She’s long talked about how happy she is to have helped keep the album format alive, as an artform and a commercial force, in the age of quick-hit streaming. But we can also guess that she’s competitive enough that the shutouts for record and song have to nag at her. They’re certainly seen as sins of omission in the world of Swifties who pay lasting and unforgiving attention to perceived snubs.
	

	Is this the year for Swift to finally make up for lost time in either Record or Song, or both? It’s fair to say she is coming into the nominating process well-armed. Of those aforementioned 15 No. 1 hits, three of them came within the eligibility period for the 2027 Grammys, which just ended — and no other artist can similarly lay a claim to three recent charttoppers. It seems like quite an advantage, having taken “The Life of Ophelia,” “Opalite” and “I Knew It, I Knew You” to the summit, all in short order,

	Except, of course, for the part where she has to pick just one.

	That’s not literally accurate; Swift or her team would be free to submit multiple entries in the same category, to put on the general ballot that will go out to Recording Academy voters on Oct. 12. But obviously she won’t, as fortune favors jockeys who don’t attempt to race astride two (or more) horses at once. So there’s a slight bit of suspense as to which of the three smashes Swift and team will place their bets on.

	Here at Variety, we are fairly certain we’ve figured out what the plan of attack will be. So jump ahead to the end if you can’t stand waiting. But if you want to know what the arguments are, here are some of the pluses and minuses Camp Swift will definitely have considered in deciding what to formally submit for election.

	“Opalite.” This is the one we can fairly safely rule out as something Swift might pick for a single submission in a top Grammy category. We render that judgment with a bit of sorrow, because Variety’s critic is on record as having chosen “Opalite” as the most ineluctably catchy and fun song of all the material on her “The Life of a Showgirl” album. If that opinion was widely shared — and we do have company in that! — this would seemingly make it a natural pick for a Record of the Year slot (if less so Song, which is more about the writing than the vibe). Yet even though it made it No. 1, an honor afforded very few songs in a calendar year, it wasn’t a multi-week No. 1. It’s just starting the race too far behind the other two tunes in terms of perceived impact.

	Why wasn’t “Opalite” a longer-lasting No. 1, when it was such a fan favorite from the moment “Showgirl” came out last October? Partly because it was a victim of the success of “Ophelia” and that song’s massive tail. Before it ever officially became a single, the streaming for “Opalite” was spread out over months and months. As an album track, it debuted at No. 2 on the Hot 100 the week “Showgirl” came out, and it remained in the top 10, on and off for 14 weeks prior to ever getting a music video or getting a radio push. But “Ophelia” was so huge, it soon became apparent that it had a shot at breaking Swift’s personal record for the most weeks one of her singles spent at No. 1, which surely was one reason why it kept getting pushed and “Opalite” kept getting pushed back. Eventually “Ophelia” hit the 10-week mark, a rare feat. When it was finally time to move on after that, “Opalite” had already been consumed in such mass quantities that it couldn’t stay on top for long. But in an alternate universe, the two “O” songs might have switched places and “Opalite” would have benefited from the more advantageous slot.
	

	“The Fate of Ophelia.” The song’s 10 weeks at No. 1 set a personal high mark for Swift, as noted above. Would anyone have picked a song named after a drowned Shakespeare character to be Swift’s longest running topper and, by some commercial standards, the biggest song of her career? She would have, and that’s the only pre-release forecasting that counts. It broke both the single-day and single-week streaming records on Spotify. But its fate was really tied to viewing as much as pure listening, thanks to a Swift-directed music video that had the star and backup dancers romping through a variety of soundstage settings, imagining her as everything from a silent-movie damsel in distress to a ’60s go-go girl.

	The real fate of “The Fate of Ophelia” wasn’t really measured in numbers, though. It was in TikTok clips and Instagram Stories and Facebook reels, etc., as the dance moves seen in the music video got memorized and charmingly copied by millions of users. Mostly by kids, yes, but some of the more novel adoptees really went viral. Moms and grandmas doing the “Ophelia” steps? Dog trainers making up modified choreography to get their German shepherds into the action? The craze had a sweetness to it. All these reenactors clearly weren’t being force-fed a hit. They were taking it to their hearts because it made them want to step lively. And anybody in the Recording Academy who either watched all those homemade clips or had a kid who did may feel that affection bubbling up again when they see “Ophelia” on their ballot.

	If they see “Ophelia” on their ballot, that is. Because we haven’t forgotten the third contender from her recent catalog, one that would seem to have equally as good a case as this to be put in front of Academy voters next month…

	“I Knew It, I Knew You.” It’s easy to tick off the reasons why Swift might choose her theme song for “Toy Story 5” over either of the songs from “The Life of a Showgirl”:

	Recency bias. Of course it’s fresher in people’s minds than “The Fate of Ophelia,” which came out early in the eligibility period last October, and will be just over a year old when voters receive their ballots in six weeks. The Disney/Pixar tune only came out in June, a full eight months later, which has to count as an advantage, even if all release dates ought to be equal. (To quote “The Fantasticks”: Try to remember / The kind of October / When that ancient autumn smash came out…)
	

	The blockbuster movie factor. A star as big as Swift can’t exactly be seen as riding another franchise’s coattails; when this single was released, the blowout unveiling created such a stir, you almost could have thought “TS5” was looking to ride hers, as much as anything. But we do have to consider that there will be Grammy voters, mostly older, who managed never to hear “Ophelia,” through Swift indifference or a general seclusion from contemporary hits, who will have been exposed to “I Knew It…” because they do not wall themselves off from the biggest or most critically appreciated movies of the year. And unless they fled for the exits at the first sign of a credit, they got a swift dose of the star at her winsomest.

	The gentle factor and the country factor. Again, older voters who find a lot of contemporary pop assaultive may have a sweet spot for a Swift song that is this easy on the ears. And her return to a country-pop sound, after so many years in a different lane, may sit well with the Nashville contingent, since she made such a concerted effort to court country radio and make it sound as if, in her heart, she’d never left. Of course, she’ll have to deal with country-inclined voters being tempted to peel off for Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” so there’s that. But after years and years of country being ignored by the Grammys in the top three categories (which Variety published a commentary about last year), it will be interesting if Swift and Langley together should offer the Academy an irresistible chance to put two country tunes among the finalists for top honors.

	Surprising longevity. “I Knew It…” hasn’t quite rivaled “Ophelia” on every numbers scale — but for just about anyone else, this might be the song of their career. The fact that “Toy Story 5” has slipped down the box-office charts a little after making a gazillion dollars has not resulted in much slippage for Swift’s song. It currently stands at No. 3 on the Hot 100, and seems pretty locked into that slot, after 12 weeks of release. Songs attached to animated films usually have a limited shelf life, but this one is showing the very rare longevity of a “We Don’t Care About Bruno” or “A Whole New World,” with a twangy twist. When home video hits, the renewal it could enjoy is anyone’s guess.
	

	She wants a damn Oscar. Well, we’re presuming… but doesn’t everybody? Perhaps the biggest factor for “I Knew It…” possibly being Swift’s pick for a Grammy campaign is that she can double it up with an Academy Awards campaign.

	The idea that “I Knew It…” might be her preference to put in front of Grammy voters certainly got a big boost when she recently appeared in front of members of the Academy’s songwriters’ wing for an exclusive, invite-only Grammy Museum appearance. In the Q&A she did with Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr., she didn’t really play any cards as far as discussing any of the eligible songs. But when she took to the piano for a climactic performance that was later released to the public on video, Swift did an Eras Tour-style mashup of three songs she felt were related, in terms of dealing with memory. “I Knew It, I Knew You” was one of those three songs. It felt like a choice.

	So which will it be?

	The verdict: A split decision. Of course, artists have the option of submitting different songs for Record and Song of the Year, although in most cases they’ll go with the same tune for both. But everything we sense about which direction Swift will go leads us to believe that she will lay different bets on both numbers, when both have so much going for them (and in the case of “I Knew It…,” still so much at stake with other awards shows).

	For Record of the Year, we prophecize that she will go with “The Fate of Ophelia.” It’s a category where bops often stand a better chance than ballads. And for Song of the Year, she can favor “I Knew It, I Knew You,” where it’s a little easier to pick out her songwriting chops from the production choices, and which has some very notable nostalgic lyricism sprinkled in among the kind of lyrics that a tyke can still reasonably grasp. There’s no real reason to think that her chances in either category would be diminished by not favoring the same song in both.

	Have we pegged this correctly? Check back Oct. 12, when the not-entirely-secret preliminary ballot goes out to voting Academy members, and we’ll know for sure whether she employed a split strategy and we really are knew-it-alls.

	[This is the first in a series of columns looking at the prospects for the 2027 Grammy Awards.]

	.

schema.headline: Taylor Swift Has Never Won a Grammy for Record or Song of the Year. With Three No. 1 Hits Eligible for 2027, Which Will She Choose for Victory?

title: Axios Co-Founders Urge Wielding AI to Help ‘Simplify’ Your Life in New Book
description:
The co-founders of Axios popularized the “Smart Brevity” mantra for years. Now, in the age of AI, comes another: “Simplify.”

	Such is the name of a
body:
The co-founders of Axios popularized the “Smart Brevity” mantra for years. Now, in the age of AI, comes another: “Simplify.”

	Such is the name of a new book by Mike Allen, Jim VandeHei and Roy Schwartz, who co-founded the political news site in 2016 to try and help get people smarter faster. “Simplify,” out Tuesday, expands on that mission, serving as an instructive guide for readers to use AI to excise distractions and boost their personal and professional lives. It’s a mantra VandeHei says worked for the company, prompting the trio over the last two and a half years to figure out how to adapt it for a tome.
	

	“I never sort of set out with, ‘Hey, I’m looking for opportunities to write a book,’” he says. “We really got inspired to write Simplify after just seeing the amazing effect it was having on our company, and also applying some of the stuff personally and seeing the effect it was having on me personally. In some ways you become almost childlike, like I want to share this with other people because it’s making such a such a huge difference.”


	The book features a mixture of anecdotes from their personal lives that detail how the three “confront” their challenges, “delete” such distractions to “amplify” their own lives. VandeHei, for example, carves out a dedicated hour for the gym every day and says no to most social functions he doesn’t deem strictly necessary, as does Allen. The latter also had to unlearn his lengthy writing habits from his days spearheading Politico’s “Playbook” newsletter for Axios’ “AM” newsletter. Schwartz, who now runs Axios’ business-focused venture Axios HQ, flipped the barrier his dyslexia provided into a tool to break down complicated topics into simple points, while MS NOW star Rachel Maddow explains her logic behind her all-black uniform for her eponymous primetime show. (“I no longer wanted to spare even the infinitesimal effort of choosing a daily variation on my standard, boring outfit,” she says in the book.)
	

	“We came to all this the hard way, and we came to it by making mistakes,” Allen says. “But the payoff for having this rigor and having this discipline is the third part of ‘amplify,’ and that’s where you cash the check for doing the hard work. That you are able to spend more time on what you’re uniquely good at, and what brings you joy.“

	AI is as much a character in the book as any of the co-founders or the company itself, reflecting Axios’ ethos that the technology will be a “moonshot” for its growth (a sentiment that came days after it laid off 11 staffers in March). The company’s enthusiastic adoption of the technology has also made its way into several columns written by VandeHei and Allen, along with a post written by publisher Nick Johnston that drew some mockery over his admission that he used AI as a guide while reading “The Last of the Mohicans.” 

	“I don’t have a lot of friends that are reading the classics at the beach,” Allen says in his defense, urging people to read the piece. “Nick is an actual book reader, and he’s someone who’s reading James Fenimore Cooper, reading ‘The Last of the Mohicans,’ reading, on paper, in hardcover, a classic, and he’s using AI as a smart friend to talk about it as he went along.”

	The co-founders warn in the book about the risk of “slop,” both human and AI-generated, interfering with the goals people set out for themselves and creating a trickle-down effect for others, leading to unnecessary work. Instead, they suggest deploying AI agents to help with everything from clearing calendars to posing questions over whether a task, menial or otherwise, is necessary.

	“There’s no hero in this story other than you,” VandeHei says. “You have to be the one who kind of really understands the technology, comes at it eyes wide open, figures out when it could be of great benefit to you. That you’re aware of the seductive nature of it, you’re aware of where you could start seeing the parts of your brain that matter most. Just like the burden in the information age on the internet was on the individual, the burden really remains on the individual.”

	Schwartz applies this mindset to his business-side clients as well, fusing AI with both “Smart Brevity” and “Simplify” approaches to, say, break down research documents for a healthcare company into bullet points so they can get the information faster. The book also ends with a QR code to help readers use an AI agent to hold themselves accountable to the “Simplify” mantra.
	

	“I hate the category of self-help, but we’ve all read those books, wanted to implement them, and had trouble implementing,” he says. “I think it’s natural, right, to not be able to hold yourself fully accountable. But AI doesn’t care.”

	VandeHei understands that the “Simplify” mindset can’t be applied universally, especially when life throws unexpected challenges in one’s way. But clearing up as much as possible in one’s life frees up more bandwidth toward some of those other tasks, which he says is ultimately the book’s goal.

	“There’s no doubt that there’s buckets of life that are inherently deep and inherently complex,” he says. “You want to be able to free up enough time so that you actually can deal with complexity when it’s required, or you can deal with depth when you need to deal with it, and so that’s why you have to simplify all the things that can be simplified. Not everything can. We’re not dumb. But the more that you can simplify — the fewer meetings, the less time wasted, the fewer projects that don’t need to be done — that gives you the time to more thoughtfully think about and take action on the things that require depth and complexity.”

title: YouTuber Allegedly Assaults Autistic College Student
body:
YouTuber
                          Assaults Autistic College Student?!?
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 9, 2026
                            2:50 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A Georgia man has been charged with abusing a disabled adult after cops say he put an autistic college student in a headlock ... before allegedly issuing a chilling threat.
      
    
            According to the police report, obtained by TMZ, Jack Tyler Laroche is accused of following a University of North Florida student into a dormitory bathroom on August 21 ... and then forcing his way into the same stall.
      
    
            The docs say Laroche started filming the man for a YouTube video before putting him in a headlock and flicking his face repeatedly, causing his glasses to fall and break.
      

            Cops say Laroche then told the student to set a 10-minute timer on his phone before leaving the bathroom ... or else he'd "come back and get you."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            At one point during the alleged bathroom encounter, cops say Laroche apparently asked for the victim's phone number and called it to confirm it was legit.
      
    
            When police eventually called Laroche's number, they say he claimed to be someone named Jack Jones who was 65 years old. When UNF police caught up with him in person, he allegedly said he was a student, Jack Jones.
      
    
            Cops say Laroche couldn't remember the name of his dorm ... before he eventually admitted his real name to authorities.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Police claim Laroche told them he was just "f***ing around" on campus to make YouTube content. He denied having any contact with the alleged victim. The alleged victim positively identified Laroche, telling campus police, "that's the person that assaulted me."
      
    
            Laroche was booked on charges of abuse of a disabled adult without causing great bodily harm, false imprisonment, and giving a false name or identification to law enforcement.
      
    
            He's since bonded out of Duval County Jail, and is expected back in court on September 14.

title: Spice Girls's Cryptic Post Has Fans Freaking Out Ahead of Big Announcement
description:
Spice Girls
                          Spice Things Up With Cryptic Tease
body:
Spice Girls
                          Spice Things Up With Cryptic Tease
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 9, 2026
                            1:46 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            It looks like the Spice Girls are about to spice up your life ... because they're definitely teasing something BIG ... and it's got folks riled up.
      
    
            Check it out ... the girl band posted a cryptic video Wednesday -- set on the same stairs from the "Wannabe" music video -- of a newspaper ad in "The Stage."
      
    
            It reads … "R U a Spice Girls fan with the ability to sing and dance? R U a superfan, a collector, a music lover? Spice Girls are a widely successful, global, choreographed, singing/dancing all female pop act with a record nine number ones in the UK and over 100 million global sales."
      
    
            It went on to say ... “No sheet music required. But you will need a vinyl or CD player."
      
    
            The ad -- printed in the same newspaper that originally published the audition ad for the Spice Girls in 1994 -- teased that whatever’s going down will be happening on September 10 at 2 PM ... so mark those calendars.
      
    
            As you know, Mel B recently shot down the idea of a reunion tour ... so fans are freaking out trying to figure out what it all means.
      
    
            Looks like only time will tell!!!
